lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: understanding a pay statement and schedule

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic understanding a pay statement and schedule task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given an annotated, entirely fictional sample pay statement with invented figures for gross pay, a few generic deduction line items, and net pay, the learner labels each part, checks the arithmetic, and writes two questions they would ask a real employer's payroll or HR contact if a real statement's line looked wrong.
safetyNotes: This is not tax, payroll, or financial advice — real pay statements vary by employer, location, and situation, and this lesson only teaches how to read the parts of a sample.
No real pay statement, real employer, or real income figure is required or should be entered anywhere.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Was your warm-up guess about gross versus net pay correct? What surprised you most about the sample statement?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Line-item accuracy: All lines are correctly labeled. | Arithmetic verification: The arithmetic correctly reconciles. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner design one additional fictional deduction line item not on the sample, add it to the statement, and recompute net pay correctly.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic understanding a pay statement and schedule task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: understanding a pay statement and schedule worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.

resources.title: understanding a pay statement and schedule action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for understanding a pay statement and schedule.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: understanding a pay statement and schedule coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given an annotated, entirely fictional sample pay statement with invented figures for gross pay, a few generic deduction line items, and net pay, the learner labels each part, checks the arithmetic, and writes two questions they would ask a real employer's payroll or HR contact if a real statement's line looked wrong.
Coach direction: Before labeling, guess what you think 'gross pay' and 'net pay' mean.
Learner prompt: In your own words, before checking, what do you think 'gross pay' and 'net pay' mean, and which one do you think is usually the bigger number?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: understanding a pay statement and schedule complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Label each line of the fictional sample pay statement.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I correctly labeled the gross pay line.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I correctly labeled each of the generic deduction line items.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I correctly labeled the net pay line.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: understanding a pay statement and schedule minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was your warm-up guess about gross versus net pay correct? What surprised you most about the sample statement?
Success checks: Line-item accuracy: All lines are correctly labeled. | Arithmetic verification: The arithmetic correctly reconciles.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: understanding a pay statement and schedule supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional understanding a pay statement and schedule condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.
Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Line-item accuracy: All lines are correctly labeled. | Arithmetic verification: The arithmetic correctly reconciles..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
